tasks.short: Compare options such as own fleet versus subcontracting, or lease versus buy, and advise on costs and financing.

steps.what: Collect request, cost, volume and flex-hour data for the options
Build cost-benefit model in Excel: NPV, payback, financing cases, sensitivities
Set assumptions, weigh risks and non-financial factors, pick recommendation
Write memo with options, numbers and recommendation

loop.input: computed option table, assumptions list, analyst's recommendation note
loop.output: draft memo with two or three options and their trade-offs
loop.check: every number in the text is matched by code against the model; mismatches block the draft
loop.stop: two redrafts, then the analyst writes the failing section
loop.why_not_simpler: a fixed template cannot explain why options differ in plain words for each request

steps.what: Present to Finance Director or site management and answer questions

tasks.design: A scheduled Python job on a governed data platform reads the nightly AFAS extract and the agency hours exports into an option data set; a standard cost-benefit template on SharePoint computes NPV, payback, lease versus Rabobank loan cases and sensitivities. A bounded model call drafts the memo from the computed table, with code checking every figure, and the analyst sets assumptions and signs off.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each request had a different shape, data sat in AFAS, agency portals and mail, and building a reusable template plus data feed cost more analyst time than the 87 hours a year it saved.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes the data feed and a parameterised template a few days of work, and models can draft option memos from a fixed table.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing assumptions (volume growth, flex rates, residual values) and pricing non-financial factors such as service risk to clients; poor source data stays poor.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which assumptions are credible for Noordhaven's sites and standing behind the recommendation in front of the Finance Director.

ambition.what: A cost-benefit check on every capex or contract request above EUR 25k, not only the large ones

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends time on assumptions and options rather than building sheets, and owns the standard cost-benefit method and its hurdle rates.

reach.learn: How approved cases flow into depreciation and the close
How lease versus buy shows up in the balance sheet and covenants

evidence.claim: Finance executives report AI more useful than expected for model building (+27) and scenario planning (+26); least useful where judgement is needed
FP&A tools let agents run scenario mechanics and draft commentary while people decide capital allocation
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt for the auditor, so the model must live in a governed place
NPV and payback in a parameterised template is standard deterministic code

assumptions: Requests come in a few recurring types (fleet, equipment, flex versus permanent staff, site investments)
The nightly AFAS extract covers the needed cost centres
unknowns: How many cost-benefit requests per year and of which types
Whether a governed data platform exists or must be set up
Hurdle rate and approval thresholds the Finance Director uses
research_questions: Do the last 20 requests fit three or four template types?
How long did each take and where did the time go?
Would the Finance Director accept a memo with options instead of one answer?
Can agency portal hours be exported on a schedule?

tasks.short: Help site and department managers with cost questions, allocations and preparing their budgets.

steps.what: Answer budget holders' questions on actuals, allocations and templates

loop.input: question in Teams, certified Power BI semantic model, budget policy on SharePoint
loop.output: draft answer with figures and source links
loop.check: figures come only from queries on the certified model; answers without a source go to the analyst
loop.stop: one query retry; unclear or new questions route to the analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: questions arrive in free Dutch text and vary too much for a fixed FAQ

steps.what: Prepare budget templates per cost centre, prefilled with actuals and run rates
Run overhead and shared-cost allocations to sites and cost centres
Check submitted budgets for errors, gaps and implausible jumps
Advise managers in meetings on budget choices and trade-offs

tasks.design: Budget templates and allocations become deterministic Python jobs on the governed data platform that read the AFAS extract and write prefilled Excel files to SharePoint, with rule checks on submissions that notify the budget holder. A Teams answer desk drafts replies from a certified Power BI semantic model and the budget policy, and the analyst approves each reply.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates and allocation keys lived in personal Excel files, and questions came by mail in free text, so nothing could answer them without the analyst.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheap coding of template and allocation jobs, and models that can turn a Dutch question into a query on a certified data model.
tasks.still_hard: Copilot in Power BI needs a prepared model and does not officially support Dutch, so the answer desk needs its own model call; allocation keys are a policy choice that managers dispute.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the managers and sites, telling a padded budget from a real need, and negotiating trade-offs.

ambition.what: Warehouse shift leaders and team leads get cost answers for their own area for the first time

tasks.altitude: Less template work and repeat mails; more time in budget conversations, and the analyst owns the allocation keys and budget check rules.

reach.task: Headcount and formation planning with managers
reach.learn: How CAO steps and flex mix drive staff cost
Which keys the close uses so budget and actuals match

evidence.claim: Budgeting is the task where finance executives report the largest positive surprise from AI (+42 net)
Copilot in Power BI answers questions on a prepared semantic model, needs F2+ or Premium capacity, and non-English use is not officially supported
Faster tools do not fix rollover budgets or padding; defined drivers and policies are needed first

assumptions: Most questions are about actuals, allocations and template use
Budget holders accept answers via Teams
unknowns: Number of budget holders and cost centres across the three sites
Current allocation keys and who approved them
Whether Fabric or Premium capacity is licensed
Whether staff-cost lines with named people appear in templates (AVG)
research_questions: What share of last year's budget questions were repeat or lookup questions?
Do managers trust a drafted answer if it links to the Power BI source?
Are allocation keys stable enough to code?
Does the works council see the answer desk as monitoring of managers?

tasks.short: Review monthly cost-centre reports against budget, find overspends and push for action.

steps.what: Pull monthly actuals per cost centre after close
Build variance tables actual versus budget and forecast
Investigate large variances: drill to invoices, agency hours, ask budget holders
Write variance commentary for the management pack

loop.input: variance table above thresholds and budget holders' explanations
loop.output: draft commentary per site and cost centre
loop.check: code matches every amount and percentage to the table; lines without a stated cause are marked 'explanation missing'
loop.stop: two attempts, then the line is left for the analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: explanations come in as free text from managers and must be summarised

steps.what: Flag overspends and agree corrective action with budget holder and controller

tasks.design: A Power BI variance report on the nightly AFAS extract replaces the monthly Excel build, with thresholds per cost centre; a scheduled job drills large variances to invoice and agency-hour lines and sends the budget holder a Teams request for a reason. A bounded model call drafts the commentary from the table and replies, and the analyst edits it and agrees actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Budget and forecast versions lived in Excel outside AFAS, and agency hours and invoices sat in three portals, so the drill-down was manual each month.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI is already in place, AI coding makes the drill-down job and threshold rules quick to build, and models can summarise manager replies.
tasks.still_hard: Budget versions must be loaded into the data platform with clean cost-centre mapping; deciding whether a variance is timing, a real overspend or a coding error still takes judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which overspends matter and pressing a site manager to act without losing the relationship.

ambition.what: Weekly expenditure check on flex-worker spend per site instead of monthly

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops building tables and spends the month on the few variances that matter, and owns the threshold and escalation rules.

reach.learn: How invoice coding errors create false variances

evidence.claim: Variance analysis shows a net +28 'more useful than expected' among finance executives
FP&A agents flag records that do not tie, do variance arithmetic and draft commentary
Commentary written after the number and unclean data are not fixed by speed
Data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance (40.4%)

assumptions: Budget and forecast exist per cost centre in a loadable format
unknowns: Where budget and forecast versions are stored today
How many cost centres and what variance thresholds are used
Whether agency portals have an API or only file export
research_questions: What share of last quarter's variances were coding or timing errors?
Do budget holders answer a Teams request faster than a mail?
Can the three agency portals be exported on a schedule?

tasks.short: Work out the staff, flex, equipment and money a new client contract or programme will need.

steps.what: Gather historical costs, volumes, FTE and flex hours for similar operations
Agree drivers with operations: volume per FTE, flex mix, shift pattern
Calculate monthly FTE, flex, equipment, opex and capex needs
Write resource plan summary with risks and ranges

loop.input: resource plan tables and driver set
loop.output: two-page summary with low, base and high cases
loop.check: code ties every figure to the plan; drivers not agreed with operations are flagged
loop.stop: two redrafts, then the analyst writes it
loop.why_not_simpler: risks and driver caveats differ per programme and need plain-language explanation

steps.what: Review the plan with operations and the Finance Director

tasks.design: A driver-based resource model in Python on the governed data platform reads the AFAS extract, agency hours and the CAO wage table, and produces monthly FTE, flex and cost needs in an Excel output on SharePoint. Headcount is held as aggregated FTE per function, not named people, and a bounded model call drafts the summary that the analyst checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drivers were never written down, so each plan was a fresh spreadsheet, and history for similar operations was spread over AFAS, agency portals and mail.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a driver model with a clean data feed affordable, and the same feed serves the budget and forecast tasks.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing realistic drivers with operations, and client volume forecasts that are often wrong; seasonal flex rates change during the year.
tasks.human_edge: Challenging operations on productivity assumptions and judging client volume risk.

ambition.what: A resource and cost estimate within two days for sales when quoting a new warehousing client

tasks.altitude: The analyst moves from assembling data to owning the driver library per site and activity, and signs off resource estimates for quotes.

reach.learn: Hiring lead times and flex-to-permanent rules in the CAO
Time to fill per function, which limits ramp-up

evidence.claim: Finance executives report net +34 for forecasting and +26 for scenario planning
Defined drivers and clean data are preconditions; speed alone repeats old errors
Headcount plans with named people are personal data under the AVG

assumptions: New client contracts or programmes arise several times a year
Operations can state productivity per activity
unknowns: How often resource plans are requested and by whom
Whether productivity data per activity exists in a warehouse system outside the listed systems
Agency rate cards and their update rhythm
Works council view on using headcount data in planning models
research_questions: Can drivers from the last three onboarding projects predict their actual costs?
Is warehouse productivity data available by site and activity?
Would sales use a two-day estimate in quotes?

role.altitude: The FP&A analysts move from assembling sheets and answering repeat questions to owning drivers, allocation keys, thresholds and the cost-benefit method, and spend their time on assumptions and conversations with site managers and the Finance Director.
reach: HR Business Partner: workforce and flex planning per site
Recruiter: time to fill as a ramp-up limit
skills_to_grow: Reading and specifying Python jobs and Power BI semantic models
Checking model-drafted text against source figures
role.ambitious_version: A monthly rolling forecast and scenarios per site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) on one governed driver model, with weekly flex-spend checks and two-day resource estimates for sales, once the drivers and data are clean.
